definition: A number $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$, where $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{i}^{2} = -1$.
The way of writing a complex number as $a + b\mathrm{i}$, real part first, with $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$.
For $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ with $a$ and $b$ real, the real number $\mathrm{Re}(z) = a$.
For $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ with $a$ and $b$ real, the real number $\mathrm{Im}(z) = b$ that multiplies $\mathrm{i}$.
For $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$, the number $z^{*} = a - b\mathrm{i}$: the reflection of $z$ in the real axis.
The distance of $z = a + b\mathrm{i}$ from the origin on an Argand diagram, $\lvert z\rvert = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}$.
The angle $\arg z$ from the positive real axis to the line from the origin to $z$, in radians, usually with $-\pi < \arg z \le \pi$.
A plane with a horizontal real axis and a vertical imaginary axis, where $a + b\mathrm{i}$ is the point $(a, b)$; also called the complex plane.
